added: The construction process can be a long, complicated, and expensive one. Depending on your level of expertise, however, you may be able to save quite a bit of money by doing some or even all of the work yourself. You can use the same fundamentals of building construction to guide you when building large, complex structures as well as small, simple ones like sheds or treehouses. Remember to adhere to all local and national laws pertaining to constructing the type of building you choose.
[[Category:House Building]]
[[Category:Commercial Real Estate]]
== Steps ==
===Planning a Successful Build===

#Identify your build site. Make sure to choose a location that is on your property and meets your specific needs. A garage needs street access, but a workshop may not. Consider what purpose the building will serve, what utilities will need to be run to it, your construction limitations, and your budget when finding a spot.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 1.jpg|center]]
#* Think about how you’ll get the concrete and lumber to your build site and if it needs vehicle access.
#* The more level the site is, the cheaper and easier it will be to prepare for building.

#Consider neighbors, sunlight, and property lines when planning the structure. If your building will have windows, you may want to orient them to get sun in the mornings or afternoons. Position the main doorway on the side of the building you’ll commonly approach it from. Develop a plan in your head for how you want the building to face and where entrances, exits, and walkways may need to be.<ref>https://www.building.govt.nz/getting-started/stages-of-the-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 2.jpg|center]]
#* If your structure will be for a business, you may want the door and large windows facing the street.
#* If you are building a garage, the garage bay door needs to be oriented toward the street as well.
#* If you are building a workshop or out-building, you may want to front door pointed at the back door of your house, since that’s where you’ll be approaching it from.

#Hire an architect or purchase a building plan. Designing a building is a complex process that is best left to the professionals. Depending on the type of building you want, you may be able to purchase off-the-shelf construction plans (for garages, outbuildings, and even houses). However, for a specialized project, you should enlist the services of an architect to ensure your building is designed to be structurally sound and within local codes.<ref>https://www.safewise.com/blog/home-building-timeline-keep-sane/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 3.jpg|center]]
#* There are websites that offer free construction plans for sheds and small structures, as well as others that sell plans for more complex buildings.
#* Many architects can create plans for buildings ranging from simple to complex, with pricing that usually matches complexity.
#* Pre-fabricated structures like sheds and even garages come with the plans and supplies you need.

#Secure the appropriate permits. There are a number of different permits you may potentially need to secure before you start construction, depending on where you live, the size of the building, and what the building will be used for. Contact your local town or city government office to inquire about building permits and how to go about getting the ones you need.<ref>[v162049_b01]. 22 September 2022.</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 4.jpg|center]]
#* Many town and city governments have websites devoted to helping you locate and apply for the correct permits.
#* Do not begin construction without securing the necessary permits, or you may be subject to legal penalties or fines.

#Use the plans to determine what work you can do yourself. Once you have a building plan, you can begin to break the project down into a sort of to-do list. You may want to do all of it yourself, or you may need to outsource some of the work to local contractors. Decide what you can and can’t do on your own beforehand so you can set up your budget. If need be, you can [[Get a Construction Loan (US)|get a construction loan]] to help pay outside work.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 5.jpg|center]]
#* The job will require building various types of framing with wood, starting with a frame for the foundation and continuing through the walls and roof.
#* You will also need to pour a large amount of concrete for the structure’s foundation, which may require the use of a concrete delivery service.
#* Wiring, HVAC, and plumbing may be concerns depending on the size and use of your building.
===Laying the Foundation===

#[[Level Ground|Level the build site]]. This process may be simple or difficult and expensive, depending on the site you’ve chosen. For small buildings, you may be able to level the site using a shovel and a tamp. However, for large buildings, you may need to use heavy machinery like a bulldozer.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 6.jpg|center]]

#* Drive stakes into the ground at all four corners of the build site, then tie a string from post to post, using a level to ensure they are perfectly straight. From there, measure the distance from the string to the ground in different spots to see how high or low they are compared to the rest. Then add or remove dirt as necessary.
#* Once the surface is even, tamp it down so it’s firm and flat.

#[[Pour a Concrete Foundation|Pour the concrete foundation]]. First, use the stakes you laid out to guide you as you install the right size lumber for your specific foundation. Different structures will have different depth requirements for the concrete, so adhere to the specifications on your building plan. Once the forms are complete, either pour the concrete yourself or hire a concrete delivery service to pour it for you.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 7.jpg|center]]

#* You can purchase concrete by the bag and mix it yourself, but for larger applications, you may want to have a concrete delivery service pour pre-mixed concrete straight into your forms from the truck.

#Add rebar or mesh to the concrete for strength. Adding the additional steel for support will strengthen the building’s foundation and reduce the chances of cracking or damage. Typically either number 4 rebar on 12 inch (30.5 cm) centers or 6X6 welded wire reinforcing wire fabric are your best options.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 8.jpg|center]]
#* You can buy either mesh or rebar at your local hardware store.
#* Insert the steel reinforcement about halfway through your pour so it will have concrete above and below it.

#Finish pouring the concrete and let it set for 24 hours. After the metal reinforcement is set, fill the wood forms the rest of the way with concrete and then brush off any excess to ensure the surface is perfectly flat.[[Image:Build a Building Step 9.jpg|center]]
#* Allow the concrete to cure for at least 24 hours before doing any more work on the structure.

#Have the site inspected if applicable. Depending on where you’re doing the construction, you may now need to have an inspector evaluate your foundation before you can set about framing the walls. If your local ordinances require an inspection, have them come once the concrete has cured.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 10.jpg|center]]
#* You can find out what inspections are necessary and how to schedule them on your local town or city government website or at City Hall.
#* Failing to schedule mandatory inspections could result in fines. The inspections are intended to ensure your structure is being built safely.
===Constructing a Shell===

#Contact your local lumber yard to help with your materials list. Instead of purchasing the wood from your local hardware store (which may not be feasible depending on the size of your project), contact your local lumber yard and use the architectural plans to place a large order of all the wood you’ll need. Many lumber yards will even deliver the order to you.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 11.jpg|center]]
#* Ordering large amounts of wood at once will reduce the overall cost.
#* Lumber yards can often help you determine exactly what you need based on your plans thanks to their experience with construction firms.

#[[Frame a Wall|Frame the exterior walls]]. On smaller buildings, build the wall first, then have friends help you raise the wall and secure it in place. On larger buildings, however, you’ll need to build the wall frames directly onto the foundation. The studs in your exterior walls should be {{convert|2|in|cm}} by {{convert|4|in|cm}}, but exterior walls on larger structures should be {{convert|2|in|cm}} by {{convert|6|in|cm}}.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_3.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 12.jpg|center]]
#* Follow the plans for your building specifically when building and placing the wall frames.
#* Pay close attention to detail while building the walls. One incorrect measurement could result in an uneven wall that could create a gap between the top of the wall and the roof.

#Add temporary wall bracing for support. Until all of the walls are completed and the roof is installed overhead, you can keep the walls standing properly by screwing temporary beams of wood into the walls that connect them to one another. These beams should be removed once you install the roof trusses.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 13.jpg|center]]
#* Use screws rather than nails so it’s easy to unscrew the braces when the structure is stable.
#* This step is often only necessary until the full frame is complete.

#[[Build a Roof|Install the roof trusses]]. You may purchase completed trusses from the lumber supply company, or you may prefer making them yourself. Roof trusses can be complex and time-consuming, so purchasing completed ones is often preferred. Attach them to the tops of the frame walls, lining up the trusses with the studs.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_3.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 14.jpg|center]]
#* Larger building may utilize a different roof framing, but trusses are the most common for small structures.

#Attach plywood to the exterior of the wall frames. Use nails to secure the plywood to the outside of the framed walls. Cut spaces in the plywood for any window or door frames. This plywood will serve as the beginning of the exterior walls.[[Image:Build a Building Step 15.jpg|center]]
#* Do not install plywood on the interior side of the walls.
#* Nail the plywood directly into the studs to secure them in place.

#Install the roof decking. You can start by nailing plywood into place on the roof to be covered and then shingled, or you may choose to [[Install Corrugated Roofing|use single piece metal roofing]] for buildings like sheds or garages. Nail or screw the decking of your choice into place along the roof trusses.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 16.jpg|center]]
#* Once done, the building will look like a nearly completed structure, but there’s still quite a bit left to do.

#Call in the inspectors. At this stage, you may need to have the building inspected again to ensure your structure is up to code. Refer to local ordinances to know for sure what inspections your specific type of building is subject to.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 17.jpg|center]]
#* The inspectors will be looking at building materials, stud spacing and signs of damage.
===Finishing the Structure===

#Run the wiring, HVAC, and plumbing through the walls. Traditionally speaking, plumbing should be done first, followed by HVAC and electrical wiring, but in practice, elements of each project will overlap. These jobs may be best left to plumbers and electricians, as they require specific skills and expertise.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 18.jpg|center]]
#* Have contractors tasked with each job work together to coordinate the installations.
#* Ensure there is no electricity flowing to the structure when working on its wiring.

#Install permanent fixtures that may affect wall placement, like bathtubs. Before the interior walls are finished, move large fixtures into place and position them where they will be once the building is complete.<Ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 19.jpg|center]]
#* It’s easier to move large things into place before all the walls are finished.
#* You’ll need to know the positioning of things like bathtubs and toilets when installing interior walls.

#Put in the insulation if applicable. Sheds and some garages are often not insulated, but if your building will be, there are a number of options to choose from. Blanket insulation is the most common for new construction and can be unrolled between the studs of the walls and stapled into place.<ref>[v162049_b01]. 22 September 2022.</ref><ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 20.jpg|center]]
#* You could also wait until the interior walls are in place and then add loose-fill or blown-in insulation into the gap between the exterior and interior walls.
#*Spray foam insulation and fiberglass insulation are alternatives.<ref>[v162049_b01]. 22 September 2022.</ref>
#* Always wear eye protection, a particulate mask, and gloves when working with fiberglass insulation.

#Staple or nail paper roofing felt to the roof if needed. If you used plywood on your roof, unroll paper roofing felt over the plywood and secure it in place. This will create a sealed barrier beneath the roofing shingles you apply.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/roof/how-to-roof-a-house/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 21.jpg|center]]
#* Cut any excess paper roofing felt off with a razor blade.
#* Make sure to staple or nail the roofing felt in place all along the perimeter to avoid it blowing up and off while you work.

#[[Lay Shingles|Nail down overlapping rows of shingles]] over the roofing felt if applicable. Start by laying a row of shingles along the roof’s bottom edge. Nail each shingle into place {{convert|2|in|cm}} from the edge and then overlap the nail with the next shingle. Then lay a second row with 6 inches (17 centimeters) behind the first one and continue until the entire roof is covered.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_5.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 22.jpg|center]]
#* Use ridge shingles on the corner created by the top point of the roof.

#[[Install Drywall|Hang drywall]] and finish the interior walls and ceiling. Measure and cut each piece of drywall, then have a friend help to put it in place. Screw the drywall into the wall studs to secure it. Then repeat that process to hang [[Install Ceiling Drywall|the ceiling drywall]] as well. Once all the drywall is in place, [[Tape and Mud Drywall|tape and mud it]] to give the drywall a smooth, paintable finish.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 23.jpg|center]]
#* Once the drywall is done, you can paint the interior walls.
#* You may also choose to cover the drywall with wallpaper.

#[[Install Vinyl Siding|Apply overlapped siding]] to the exterior of the building. Overlapping siding works just like roof shingles to protect the exterior wall of your building. Start by installing a starter strip and corner posts using nails, then cut and install layers of siding to the walls starting at the bottom.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_5.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 24.jpg|center]]
#* Overlap adjoining panels of siding to prevent moisture from getting in.

Depending on your level of expertise, however, you may be able to save quite a bit of money by doing some or even all of the work yourself. You can use the same fundamentals of building construction to guide you when building large, complex structures as well as small, simple ones like sheds or treehouses. Remember to adhere to all local and national laws pertaining to constructing the type of building you choose.

== Steps ==
===Planning a Successful Build===

#Identify your build site. Make sure to choose a location that is on your property and meets your specific needs. A garage needs street access, but a workshop may not. Consider what purpose the building will serve, what utilities will need to be run to it, your construction limitations, and your budget when finding a spot.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 1.jpg|center]]
#* Think about how you’ll get the concrete and lumber to your build site and if it needs vehicle access.
#* The more level the site is, the cheaper and easier it will be to prepare for building.

#Consider neighbors, sunlight, and property lines when planning the structure. If your building will have windows, you may want to orient them to get sun in the mornings or afternoons. Position the main doorway on the side of the building you’ll commonly approach it from. Develop a plan in your head for how you want the building to face and where entrances, exits, and walkways may need to be.<ref>https://www.building.govt.nz/getting-started/stages-of-the-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 2.jpg|center]]
#* If your structure will be for a business, you may want the door and large windows facing the street.
#* If you are building a garage, the garage bay door needs to be oriented toward the street as well.
#* If you are building a workshop or out-building, you may want to front door pointed at the back door of your house, since that’s where you’ll be approaching it from.

#Hire an architect or purchase a building plan. Designing a building is a complex process that is best left to the professionals. Depending on the type of building you want, you may be able to purchase off-the-shelf construction plans (for garages, outbuildings, and even houses). However, for a specialized project, you should enlist the services of an architect to ensure your building is designed to be structurally sound and within local codes.<ref>https://www.safewise.com/blog/home-building-timeline-keep-sane/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 3.jpg|center]]
#* There are websites that offer free construction plans for sheds and small structures, as well as others that sell plans for more complex buildings.
#* Many architects can create plans for buildings ranging from simple to complex, with pricing that usually matches complexity.
#* Pre-fabricated structures like sheds and even garages come with the plans and supplies you need.

#Secure the appropriate permits. There are a number of different permits you may potentially need to secure before you start construction, depending on where you live, the size of the building, and what the building will be used for. Contact your local town or city government office to inquire about building permits and how to go about getting the ones you need.<ref>[v162049_b01]. 22 September 2022.</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 4.jpg|center]]
#* Many town and city governments have websites devoted to helping you locate and apply for the correct permits.
#* Do not begin construction without securing the necessary permits, or you may be subject to legal penalties or fines.

#Use the plans to determine what work you can do yourself. Once you have a building plan, you can begin to break the project down into a sort of to-do list. You may want to do all of it yourself, or you may need to outsource some of the work to local contractors. Decide what you can and can’t do on your own beforehand so you can set up your budget. If need be, you can [[Get a Construction Loan (US)|get a construction loan]] to help pay outside work.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 5.jpg|center]]

#* You will also need to pour a large amount of concrete for the structure’s foundation, which may require the use of a concrete delivery service.
#* Wiring, HVAC, and plumbing may be concerns depending on the size and use of your building.
===Laying the Foundation===

#[[Level Ground|Level the build site]]. This process may be simple or difficult and expensive, depending on the site you’ve chosen. For small buildings, you may be able to level the site using a shovel and a tamp. However, for large buildings, you may need to use heavy machinery like a bulldozer.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 6.jpg|center]]

#* Drive stakes into the ground at all four corners of the build site, then tie a string from post to post, using a level to ensure they are perfectly straight. From there, measure the distance from the string to the ground in different spots to see how high or low they are compared to the rest. Then add or remove dirt as necessary.

#Add temporary wall bracing for support. Until all of the walls are completed and the roof is installed overhead, you can keep the walls standing properly by screwing temporary beams of wood into the walls that connect them to one another. These beams should be removed once you install the roof trusses.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 13.jpg|center]]
#* Use screws rather than nails so it’s easy to unscrew the braces when the structure is stable.
#* This step is often only necessary until the full frame is complete.

Roof trusses can be complex and time-consuming, so purchasing completed ones is often preferred. Attach them to the tops of the frame walls, lining up the trusses with the studs.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_3.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 14.jpg|center]]

#* Do not install plywood on the interior side of the walls.
#* Nail the plywood directly into the studs to secure them in place.

You can start by nailing plywood into place on the roof to be covered and then shingled, or you may choose to [[Install Corrugated Roofing|use single piece metal roofing]] for buildings like sheds or garages. Nail or screw the decking of your choice into place along the roof trusses.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 16.jpg|center]]
#* Once done, the building will look like a nearly completed structure, but there’s still quite a bit left to do.

Refer to local ordinances to know for sure what inspections your specific type of building is subject to.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 17.jpg|center]]
#* The inspectors will be looking at building materials, stud spacing and signs of damage.

Traditionally speaking, plumbing should be done first, followed by HVAC and electrical wiring, but in practice, elements of each project will overlap. #* Ensure there is no electricity flowing to the structure when working on its wiring.

Before the interior walls are finished, move large fixtures into place and position them where they will be once the building is complete.<Ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 19.jpg|center]]

Overview of Pre-Engineered Buildings

Pre-engineered buildings consist of a steel framework designed to carry loads efficiently and optimize the use of materials. Unlike conventional construction, where raw materials are brought to the site for on-site fabrication, PEBs are manufactured in a controlled factory environment. This approach ensures high precision, consistent quality, and reduced construction timelines.
Key advantages of PEBs include:
Faster Construction: Pre-fabricated components reduce on-site assembly time.
Cost Efficiency: Optimized steel usage and factory fabrication reduce waste.
Design Flexibility: Structures can be customized to meet specific height, width, and functional requirements.
Durability: Steel frameworks provide high strength-to-weight ratios and long-term reliability.

The Indian construction sector has witnessed steady growth in PEB adoption due to:
Industrial Expansion: Manufacturing facilities, warehouses, and factories require large-span structures that PEBs provide efficiently.

Technological Advancements: Modern design software and fabrication techniques improve structural accuracy and reduce costs.

Sports and Recreational Facilities: Stadiums, gyms, and indoor arenas.

== Steps ==
===Planning a Successful Build===

#Identify your build site. Make sure to choose a location that is on your property and meets your specific needs. A garage needs street access, but a workshop may not. Consider what purpose the building will serve, what utilities will need to be run to it, your construction limitations, and your budget when finding a spot.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 1.jpg|center]]
#* Think about how you’ll get the concrete and lumber to your build site and if it needs vehicle access.
#* The more level the site is, the cheaper and easier it will be to prepare for building.

#Consider neighbors, sunlight, and property lines when planning the structure. If your building will have windows, you may want to orient them to get sun in the mornings or afternoons. Position the main doorway on the side of the building you’ll commonly approach it from. Develop a plan in your head for how you want the building to face and where entrances, exits, and walkways may need to be.<ref>https://www.building.govt.nz/getting-started/stages-of-the-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 2.jpg|center]]
#* If your structure will be for a business, you may want the door and large windows facing the street.
#* If you are building a garage, the garage bay door needs to be oriented toward the street as well.
#* If you are building a workshop or out-building, you may want to front door pointed at the back door of your house, since that’s where you’ll be approaching it from.

#Hire an architect or purchase a building plan. Designing a building is a complex process that is best left to the professionals. Depending on the type of building you want, you may be able to purchase off-the-shelf construction plans (for garages, outbuildings, and even houses). However, for a specialized project, you should enlist the services of an architect to ensure your building is designed to be structurally sound and within local codes.<ref>https://www.safewise.com/blog/home-building-timeline-keep-sane/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 3.jpg|center]]
#* There are websites that offer free construction plans for sheds and small structures, as well as others that sell plans for more complex buildings.
#* Many architects can create plans for buildings ranging from simple to complex, with pricing that usually matches complexity.
#* Pre-fabricated structures like sheds and even garages come with the plans and supplies you need.

#Secure the appropriate permits. There are a number of different permits you may potentially need to secure before you start construction, depending on where you live, the size of the building, and what the building will be used for. Contact your local town or city government office to inquire about building permits and how to go about getting the ones you need.<ref>[v162049_b01]. 22 September 2022.</ref><Ref>http://www.catawbacountync.gov/building/pc_QApermits.asp?mode=ddmenu</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 4.jpg|center]]
#* Many town and city governments have websites devoted to helping you locate and apply for the correct permits.
#* Do not begin construction without securing the necessary permits, or you may be subject to legal penalties or fines.

#Use the plans to determine what work you can do yourself. Once you have a building plan, you can begin to break the project down into a sort of to-do list. You may want to do all of it yourself, or you may need to outsource some of the work to local contractors. Decide what you can and can’t do on your own beforehand so you can set up your budget. If need be, you can [[Get a Construction Loan (US)|get a construction loan]] to help pay outside work.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 5.jpg|center]]
#* The job will require building various types of framing with wood, starting with a frame for the foundation and continuing through the walls and roof.
#* You will also need to pour a large amount of concrete for the structure’s foundation, which may require the use of a concrete delivery service.
#* Wiring, HVAC, and plumbing may be concerns depending on the size and use of your building.
===Laying the Foundation===

#[[Level Ground|Level the build site]]. This process may be simple or difficult and expensive, depending on the site you’ve chosen. For small buildings, you may be able to level the site using a shovel and a tamp. However, for large buildings, you may need to use heavy machinery like a bulldozer.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 6.jpg|center]]

#* Drive stakes into the ground at all four corners of the build site, then tie a string from post to post, using a level to ensure they are perfectly straight. From there, measure the distance from the string to the ground in different spots to see how high or low they are compared to the rest. Then add or remove dirt as necessary.
#* Once the surface is even, tamp it down so it’s firm and flat.

#[[Pour a Concrete Foundation|Pour the concrete foundation]]. First, use the stakes you laid out to guide you as you install the right size lumber for your specific foundation. Different structures will have different depth requirements for the concrete, so adhere to the specifications on your building plan. Once the forms are complete, either pour the concrete yourself or hire a concrete delivery service to pour it for you.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 7.jpg|center]]

#* You can purchase concrete by the bag and mix it yourself, but for larger applications, you may want to have a concrete delivery service pour pre-mixed concrete straight into your forms from the truck.

#Add rebar or mesh to the concrete for strength. Adding the additional steel for support will strengthen the building’s foundation and reduce the chances of cracking or damage. Typically either number 4 rebar on 12 inch (30.5 cm) centers or 6X6 welded wire reinforcing wire fabric are your best options.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 8.jpg|center]]
#* You can buy either mesh or rebar at your local hardware store.
#* Insert the steel reinforcement about halfway through your pour so it will have concrete above and below it.

#Finish pouring the concrete and let it set for 24 hours. After the metal reinforcement is set, fill the wood forms the rest of the way with concrete and then brush off any excess to ensure the surface is perfectly flat.[[Image:Build a Building Step 9.jpg|center]]
#* Allow the concrete to cure for at least 24 hours before doing any more work on the structure.

#Have the site inspected if applicable. Depending on where you’re doing the construction, you may now need to have an inspector evaluate your foundation before you can set about framing the walls. If your local ordinances require an inspection, have them come once the concrete has cured.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 10.jpg|center]]
#* You can find out what inspections are necessary and how to schedule them on your local town or city government website or at City Hall.
#* Failing to schedule mandatory inspections could result in fines. The inspections are intended to ensure your structure is being built safely.
===Constructing a Shell===

#Contact your local lumber yard to help with your materials list. Instead of purchasing the wood from your local hardware store (which may not be feasible depending on the size of your project), contact your local lumber yard and use the architectural plans to place a large order of all the wood you’ll need. Many lumber yards will even deliver the order to you.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 11.jpg|center]]
#* Ordering large amounts of wood at once will reduce the overall cost.
#* Lumber yards can often help you determine exactly what you need based on your plans thanks to their experience with construction firms.

#[[Frame a Wall|Frame the exterior walls]]. On smaller buildings, build the wall first, then have friends help you raise the wall and secure it in place. On larger buildings, however, you’ll need to build the wall frames directly onto the foundation. The studs in your exterior walls should be {{convert|2|in|cm}} by {{convert|4|in|cm}}, but exterior walls on larger structures should be {{convert|2|in|cm}} by {{convert|6|in|cm}}.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_3.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 12.jpg|center]]
#* Follow the plans for your building specifically when building and placing the wall frames.
#* Pay close attention to detail while building the walls. One incorrect measurement could result in an uneven wall that could create a gap between the top of the wall and the roof.

#Add temporary wall bracing for support. Until all of the walls are completed and the roof is installed overhead, you can keep the walls standing properly by screwing temporary beams of wood into the walls that connect them to one another. These beams should be removed once you install the roof trusses.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 13.jpg|center]]
#* Use screws rather than nails so it’s easy to unscrew the braces when the structure is stable.
#* This step is often only necessary until the full frame is complete.

#[[Build a Roof|Install the roof trusses]]. You may purchase completed trusses from the lumber supply company, or you may prefer making them yourself. Roof trusses can be complex and time-consuming, so purchasing completed ones is often preferred. Attach them to the tops of the frame walls, lining up the trusses with the studs.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_3.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 14.jpg|center]]
#* Larger building may utilize a different roof framing, but trusses are the most common for small structures.

#Attach plywood to the exterior of the wall frames. Use nails to secure the plywood to the outside of the framed walls. Cut spaces in the plywood for any window or door frames. This plywood will serve as the beginning of the exterior walls.[[Image:Build a Building Step 15.jpg|center]]
#* Do not install plywood on the interior side of the walls.
#* Nail the plywood directly into the studs to secure them in place.

#Install the roof decking. You can start by nailing plywood into place on the roof to be covered and then shingled, or you may choose to [[Install Corrugated Roofing|use single piece metal roofing]] for buildings like sheds or garages. Nail or screw the decking of your choice into place along the roof trusses.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 16.jpg|center]]
#* Once done, the building will look like a nearly completed structure, but there’s still quite a bit left to do.

#Call in the inspectors. At this stage, you may need to have the building inspected again to ensure your structure is up to code. Refer to local ordinances to know for sure what inspections your specific type of building is subject to.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 17.jpg|center]]
#* The inspectors will be looking at building materials, stud spacing and signs of damage.
===Finishing the Structure===

#Run the wiring, HVAC, and plumbing through the walls. Traditionally speaking, plumbing should be done first, followed by HVAC and electrical wiring, but in practice, elements of each project will overlap. These jobs may be best left to plumbers and electricians, as they require specific skills and expertise.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 18.jpg|center]]
#* Have contractors tasked with each job work together to coordinate the installations.
#* Ensure there is no electricity flowing to the structure when working on its wiring.

#Install permanent fixtures that may affect wall placement, like bathtubs. Before the interior walls are finished, move large fixtures into place and position them where they will be once the building is complete.<Ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 19.jpg|center]]
#* It’s easier to move large things into place before all the walls are finished.
#* You’ll need to know the positioning of things like bathtubs and toilets when installing interior walls.

#Put in the insulation if applicable. Sheds and some garages are often not insulated, but if your building will be, there are a number of options to choose from. Blanket insulation is the most common for new construction and can be unrolled between the studs of the walls and stapled into place.<ref>[v162049_b01]. 22 September 2022.</ref><ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 20.jpg|center]]
#* You could also wait until the interior walls are in place and then add loose-fill or blown-in insulation into the gap between the exterior and interior walls.
#*Spray foam insulation and fiberglass insulation are alternatives.<ref>[v162049_b01]. 22 September 2022.</ref>
#* Always wear eye protection, a particulate mask, and gloves when working with fiberglass insulation.

#Staple or nail paper roofing felt to the roof if needed. If you used plywood on your roof, unroll paper roofing felt over the plywood and secure it in place. This will create a sealed barrier beneath the roofing shingles you apply.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/roof/how-to-roof-a-house/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 21.jpg|center]]
#* Cut any excess paper roofing felt off with a razor blade.
#* Make sure to staple or nail the roofing felt in place all along the perimeter to avoid it blowing up and off while you work.

#[[Lay Shingles|Nail down overlapping rows of shingles]] over the roofing felt if applicable. Start by laying a row of shingles along the roof’s bottom edge. Nail each shingle into place {{convert|2|in|cm}} from the edge and then overlap the nail with the next shingle. Then lay a second row with 6 inches (17 centimeters) behind the first one and continue until the entire roof is covered.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_5.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 22.jpg|center]]
#* Use ridge shingles on the corner created by the top point of the roof.

#[[Install Drywall|Hang drywall]] and finish the interior walls and ceiling. Measure and cut each piece of drywall, then have a friend help to put it in place. Screw the drywall into the wall studs to secure it. Then repeat that process to hang [[Install Ceiling Drywall|the ceiling drywall]] as well. Once all the drywall is in place, [[Tape and Mud Drywall|tape and mud it]] to give the drywall a smooth, paintable finish.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/learn/step-by-step-guide-to-home-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 23.jpg|center]]
#* Once the drywall is done, you can paint the interior walls.
#* You may also choose to cover the drywall with wallpaper.

#[[Install Vinyl Siding|Apply overlapped siding]] to the exterior of the building. Overlapping siding works just like roof shingles to protect the exterior wall of your building. Start by installing a starter strip and corner posts using nails, then cut and install layers of siding to the walls starting at the bottom.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_5.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 24.jpg|center]]
#* Overlap adjoining panels of siding to prevent moisture from getting in.

#Attach plywood to the exterior of the wall frames. Use nails to secure the plywood to the outside of the framed walls. Cut spaces in the plywood for any window or door frames. This plywood will serve as the beginning of the exterior walls.[[Image:Build a Building Step 15.jpg|center]]

#Call in the inspectors. At this stage, you may need to have the building inspected again to ensure your structure is up to code. #Run the wiring, HVAC, and plumbing through the walls. Traditionally speaking, plumbing should be done first, followed by HVAC and electrical wiring, but in practice, elements of each project will overlap. These jobs may be best left to plumbers and electricians, as they require specific skills and expertise.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 18.jpg|center]]
#* Have contractors tasked with each job work together to coordinate the installations.
#* Ensure there is no electricity flowing to the structure when working on its wiring.

#Install permanent fixtures that may affect wall placement, like bathtubs. Before the interior walls are finished, move large fixtures into place and position them where they will be once the building is complete.<Ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 19.jpg|center]]
#* It’s easier to move large things into place before all the walls are finished.
#* You’ll need to know the positioning of things like bathtubs and toilets when installing interior walls.

#Put in the insulation if applicable. Sheds and some garages are often not insulated, but if your building will be, there are a number of options to choose from. Blanket insulation is the most common for new construction and can be unrolled between the studs of the walls and stapled into place.<ref>[v162049_b01]. 22 September 2022.</ref><ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 20.jpg|center]]

#*Spray foam insulation and fiberglass insulation are alternatives.<ref>[v162049_b01]. 22 September 2022.</ref>

#Staple or nail paper roofing felt to the roof if needed. If you used plywood on your roof, unroll paper roofing felt over the plywood and secure it in place. This will create a sealed barrier beneath the roofing shingles you apply.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/roof/how-to-roof-a-house/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 21.jpg|center]]

Nail each shingle into place {{convert|2|in|cm}} from the edge and then overlap the nail with the next shingle. #* If your structure will be for a business, you may want the door and large windows facing the street.
#* If you are building a garage, the garage bay door needs to be oriented toward the street as well.
#* If you are building a workshop or out-building, you may want to front door pointed at the back door of your house, since that’s where you’ll be approaching it from.

#Hire an architect or purchase a building plan. Designing a building is a complex process that is best left to the professionals. #* There are websites that offer free construction plans for sheds and small structures, as well as others that sell plans for more complex buildings.
#* Many architects can create plans for buildings ranging from simple to complex, with pricing that usually matches complexity.
#* Pre-fabricated structures like sheds and even garages come with the plans and supplies you need.

#Secure the appropriate permits. There are a number of different permits you may potentially need to secure before you start construction, depending on where you live, the size of the building, and what the building will be used for. #* Many town and city governments have websites devoted to helping you locate and apply for the correct permits.
#* Do not begin construction without securing the necessary permits, or you may be subject to legal penalties or fines.

#* You will also need to pour a large amount of concrete for the structure’s foundation, which may require the use of a concrete delivery service.
#* Wiring, HVAC, and plumbing may be concerns depending on the size and use of your building.

#[[Level Ground|Level the build site]]. This process may be simple or difficult and expensive, depending on the site you’ve chosen. == Steps ==
===Planning a Successful Build===

#Identify your build site. Make sure to choose a location that is on your property and meets your specific needs. A garage needs street access, but a workshop may not. Consider what purpose the building will serve, what utilities will need to be run to it, your construction limitations, and your budget when finding a spot.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 1.jpg|center]]
#* Think about how you’ll get the concrete and lumber to your build site and if it needs vehicle access.
#* The more level the site is, the cheaper and easier it will be to prepare for building.

#Consider neighbors, sunlight, and property lines when planning the structure. If your building will have windows, you may want to orient them to get sun in the mornings or afternoons. Position the main doorway on the side of the building you’ll commonly approach it from. Develop a plan in your head for how you want the building to face and where entrances, exits, and walkways may need to be.<ref>https://www.building.govt.nz/getting-started/stages-of-the-building-process/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 2.jpg|center]]
#* If your structure will be for a business, you may want the door and large windows facing the street.
#* If you are building a garage, the garage bay door needs to be oriented toward the street as well.
#* If you are building a workshop or out-building, you may want to front door pointed at the back door of your house, since that’s where you’ll be approaching it from.

#Hire an architect or purchase a building plan. Designing a building is a complex process that is best left to the professionals. Depending on the type of building you want, you may be able to purchase off-the-shelf construction plans (for garages, outbuildings, and even houses). However, for a specialized project, you should enlist the services of an architect to ensure your building is designed to be structurally sound and within local codes.<ref>https://www.safewise.com/blog/home-building-timeline-keep-sane/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 3.jpg|center]]
#* There are websites that offer free construction plans for sheds and small structures, as well as others that sell plans for more complex buildings.
#* Many architects can create plans for buildings ranging from simple to complex, with pricing that usually matches complexity.
#* Pre-fabricated structures like sheds and even garages come with the plans and supplies you need.

#Secure the appropriate permits. There are a number of different permits you may potentially need to secure before you start construction, depending on where you live, the size of the building, and what the building will be used for. Contact your local town or city government office to inquire about building permits and how to go about getting the ones you need.<Ref>http://www.catawbacountync.gov/building/pc_QApermits.asp?mode=ddmenu</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 4.jpg|center]]
#* Many town and city governments have websites devoted to helping you locate and apply for the correct permits.
#* Do not begin construction without securing the necessary permits, or you may be subject to legal penalties or fines.

#Use the plans to determine what work you can do yourself. Once you have a building plan, you can begin to break the project down into a sort of to-do list. You may want to do all of it yourself, or you may need to outsource some of the work to local contractors. Decide what you can and can’t do on your own beforehand so you can set up your budget. If need be, you can [[Get a Construction Loan (US)|get a construction loan]] to help pay outside work.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 5.jpg|center]]
#* The job will require building various types of framing with wood, starting with a frame for the foundation and continuing through the walls and roof.
#* You will also need to pour a large amount of concrete for the structure’s foundation, which may require the use of a concrete delivery service.
#* Wiring, HVAC, and plumbing may be concerns depending on the size and use of your building.
===Laying the Foundation===

#[[Level Ground|Level the build site]]. This process may be simple or difficult and expensive, depending on the site you’ve chosen. For small buildings, you may be able to level the site using a shovel and a tamp. However, for large buildings, you may need to use heavy machinery like a bulldozer.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 6.jpg|center]]

#* Drive stakes into the ground at all four corners of the build site, then tie a string from post to post, using a level to ensure they are perfectly straight. From there, measure the distance from the string to the ground in different spots to see how high or low they are compared to the rest. Then add or remove dirt as necessary.
#* Once the surface is even, tamp it down so it’s firm and flat.

#[[Pour a Concrete Foundation|Pour the concrete foundation]]. First, use the stakes you laid out to guide you as you install the right size lumber for your specific foundation. Different structures will have different depth requirements for the concrete, so adhere to the specifications on your building plan. Once the forms are complete, either pour the concrete yourself or hire a concrete delivery service to pour it for you.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 7.jpg|center]]

#* You can purchase concrete by the bag and mix it yourself, but for larger applications, you may want to have a concrete delivery service pour pre-mixed concrete straight into your forms from the truck.

#Add rebar or mesh to the concrete for strength. Adding the additional steel for support will strengthen the building’s foundation and reduce the chances of cracking or damage. Typically either number 4 rebar on 12 inch (30.5 cm) centers or 6X6 welded wire reinforcing wire fabric are your best options.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 8.jpg|center]]
#* You can buy either mesh or rebar at your local hardware store.
#* Insert the steel reinforcement about halfway through your pour so it will have concrete above and below it.

#Finish pouring the concrete and let it set for 24 hours. After the metal reinforcement is set, fill the wood forms the rest of the way with concrete and then brush off any excess to ensure the surface is perfectly flat.[[Image:Build a Building Step 9.jpg|center]]
#* Allow the concrete to cure for at least 24 hours before doing any more work on the structure.

#Have the site inspected if applicable. Depending on where you’re doing the construction, you may now need to have an inspector evaluate your foundation before you can set about framing the walls. If your local ordinances require an inspection, have them come once the concrete has cured.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 10.jpg|center]]
#* You can find out what inspections are necessary and how to schedule them on your local town or city government website or at City Hall.
#* Failing to schedule mandatory inspections could result in fines. The inspections are intended to ensure your structure is being built safely.
===Constructing a Shell===

#Contact your local lumber yard to help with your materials list. Instead of purchasing the wood from your local hardware store (which may not be feasible depending on the size of your project), contact your local lumber yard and use the architectural plans to place a large order of all the wood you’ll need. Many lumber yards will even deliver the order to you.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 11.jpg|center]]
#* Ordering large amounts of wood at once will reduce the overall cost.
#* Lumber yards can often help you determine exactly what you need based on your plans thanks to their experience with construction firms.

#[[Frame a Wall|Frame the exterior walls]]. On smaller buildings, build the wall first, then have friends help you raise the wall and secure it in place. On larger buildings, however, you’ll need to build the wall frames directly onto the foundation. The studs in your exterior walls should be {{convert|2|in|cm}} by {{convert|4|in|cm}}, but exterior walls on larger structures should be {{convert|2|in|cm}} by {{convert|6|in|cm}}.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_3.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 12.jpg|center]]
#* Follow the plans for your building specifically when building and placing the wall frames.
#* Pay close attention to detail while building the walls. One incorrect measurement could result in an uneven wall that could create a gap between the top of the wall and the roof.

#Add temporary wall bracing for support. Until all of the walls are completed and the roof is installed overhead, you can keep the walls standing properly by screwing temporary beams of wood into the walls that connect them to one another. These beams should be removed once you install the roof trusses.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 13.jpg|center]]
#* Use screws rather than nails so it’s easy to unscrew the braces when the structure is stable.
#* This step is often only necessary until the full frame is complete.

#[[Build a Roof|Install the roof trusses]]. You may purchase completed trusses from the lumber supply company, or you may prefer making them yourself. Roof trusses can be complex and time-consuming, so purchasing completed ones is often preferred. Attach them to the tops of the frame walls, lining up the trusses with the studs.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_3.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 14.jpg|center]]
#* Larger building may utilize a different roof framing, but trusses are the most common for small structures.

#Attach plywood to the exterior of the wall frames. Use nails to secure the plywood to the outside of the framed walls. Cut spaces in the plywood for any window or door frames. This plywood will serve as the beginning of the exterior walls.[[Image:Build a Building Step 15.jpg|center]]
#* Do not install plywood on the interior side of the walls.
#* Nail the plywood directly into the studs to secure them in place.

#Install the roof decking. You can start by nailing plywood into place on the roof to be covered and then shingled, or you may choose to [[Install Corrugated Roofing|use single piece metal roofing]] for buildings like sheds or garages. Nail or screw the decking of your choice into place along the roof trusses.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/garage/framing-a-garage/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 16.jpg|center]]
#* Once done, the building will look like a nearly completed structure, but there’s still quite a bit left to do.

#Call in the inspectors. At this stage, you may need to have the building inspected again to ensure your structure is up to code. Refer to local ordinances to know for sure what inspections your specific type of building is subject to.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 17.jpg|center]]
#* The inspectors will be looking at building materials, stud spacing and signs of damage.
===Finishing the Structure===

#Run the wiring, HVAC, and plumbing through the walls. Traditionally speaking, plumbing should be done first, followed by HVAC and electrical wiring, but in practice, elements of each project will overlap. These jobs may be best left to plumbers and electricians, as they require specific skills and expertise.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 18.jpg|center]]
#* Have contractors tasked with each job work together to coordinate the installations.
#* Ensure there is no electricity flowing to the structure when working on its wiring.

#Install permanent fixtures that may affect wall placement, like bathtubs. Before the interior walls are finished, move large fixtures into place and position them where they will be once the building is complete.<Ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 19.jpg|center]]
#* It’s easier to move large things into place before all the walls are finished.
#* You’ll need to know the positioning of things like bathtubs and toilets when installing interior walls.

#Put in the insulation if applicable. Sheds and some garages are often not insulated, but if your building will be, there are a number of options to choose from. Blanket insulation is the most common for new construction and can be unrolled between the studs of the walls and stapled into place.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 20.jpg|center]]
#* You could also wait until the interior walls are in place and then add loose-fill or blown-in insulation into the gap between the exterior and interior walls.
#* Always wear eye protection, a particulate mask, and gloves when working with fiberglass insulation.

#Staple or nail paper roofing felt to the roof if needed. If you used plywood on your roof, unroll paper roofing felt over the plywood and secure it in place. This will create a sealed barrier beneath the roofing shingles you apply.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/roof/how-to-roof-a-house/view-all/</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 21.jpg|center]]
#* Cut any excess paper roofing felt off with a razor blade.
#* Make sure to staple or nail the roofing felt in place all along the perimeter to avoid it blowing up and off while you work.

#[[Lay Shingles|Nail down overlapping rows of shingles]] over the roofing felt if applicable. Start by laying a row of shingles along the roof’s bottom edge. Nail each shingle into place {{convert|2|in|cm}} from the edge and then overlap the nail with the next shingle. Then lay a second row with 6 inches (17 centimeters) behind the first one and continue until the entire roof is covered.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_5.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 22.jpg|center]]
#* Use ridge shingles on the corner created by the top point of the roof.

#[[Install Drywall|Hang drywall]] and finish the interior walls and ceiling. Measure and cut each piece of drywall, then have a friend help to put it in place. Screw the drywall into the wall studs to secure it. Then repeat that process to hang [[Install Ceiling Drywall|the ceiling drywall]] as well. Once all the drywall is in place, [[Tape and Mud Drywall|tape and mud it]] to give the drywall a smooth, paintable finish.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 23.jpg|center]]
#* Once the drywall is done, you can paint the interior walls.
#* You may also choose to cover the drywall with wallpaper.

#[[Install Vinyl Siding|Apply overlapped siding]] to the exterior of the building. Overlapping siding works just like roof shingles to protect the exterior wall of your building. Start by installing a starter strip and corner posts using nails, then cut and install layers of siding to the walls starting at the bottom.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_5.htm</ref>[[Image:Build a Building Step 24.jpg|center]]
#* Overlap adjoining panels of siding to prevent moisture from getting in.
== Tips ==

*You’ll usually need to have inspections done after laying the concrete foundation, installing the floors, and after putting up the external walls and roof. Other inspections may be specified by local laws and regulations.

#* Always wear eye protection, a particulate mask, and gloves when working with fiberglass insulation.

#Staple or nail paper roofing felt to the roof if needed. If you used plywood on your roof, unroll paper roofing felt over the plywood and secure it in place. This will create a sealed barrier beneath the roofing shingles you apply.<ref>https://www.familyhandyman.com/roof/how-to-roof-a-house/view-all/</ref>
#* Cut any excess paper roofing felt off with a razor blade.
#* Make sure to staple or nail the roofing felt in place all along the perimeter to avoid it blowing up and off while you work.

#[[Lay Shingles|Nail down overlapping rows of shingles]] over the roofing felt if applicable. Start by laying a row of shingles along the roof’s bottom edge. Nail each shingle into place {{convert|2|in|cm}} from the edge and then overlap the nail with the next shingle. Then lay a second row with 6 inches (17 centimeters) behind the first one and continue until the entire roof is covered.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_5.htm</ref>
#* Use ridge shingles on the corner created by the top point of the roof.

#[[Install Drywall|Hang drywall]] and finish the interior walls and ceiling. Measure and cut each piece of drywall, then have a friend help to put it in place. Screw the drywall into the wall studs to secure it. Then repeat that process to hang [[Install Ceiling Drywall|the ceiling drywall]] as well. Once all the drywall is in place, [[Tape and Mud Drywall|tape and mud it]] to give the drywall a smooth, paintable finish.<ref>https://www.newhomesource.com/guide/articles/a-step-by-step-guide-to-the-home-building-process</ref>
#* Once the drywall is done, you can paint the interior walls.
#* You may also choose to cover the drywall with wallpaper.

#[[Install Vinyl Siding|Apply overlapped siding]] to the exterior of the building. Overlapping siding works just like roof shingles to protect the exterior wall of your building. Start by installing a starter strip and corner posts using nails, then cut and install layers of siding to the walls starting at the bottom.<ref>http://www.hometime.com/Howto/projects/garage/garage_5.htm</ref>
#* Overlap adjoining panels of siding to prevent moisture from getting in.
